verification_notes: Audited from first principles: Misconception that Total Internal Reflection can occur when entering a denser medium verified. Snell's Law sin(r) = (n_1 / n_2)*sin(i). When n_1 < n_2 (rarer to denser), n_1 / n_2 < 1. Since sin(i) <= 1, sin(r) <= n_1 / n_2 < 1 for all physical angles of incidence i. Thus, the angle of refraction r is always real and strictly bounded by r_max = arcsin(n_1 / n_2) < 90 degrees. TIR requires sin(r) > 1, which is mathematically impossible when n_1 < n_2. Physical refutation, mathematical counter-proof, and corrective pedagogical exposition verified.
